body_markdown:
As far as moonshot pickups go, American automotive history has its fair share of notable contenders. Whether you reach all the way back for something like the Dodge Lil’ Red Express, a small-but-mighty[GMC Syclone](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/perfect-storms-the-gmc-syclone-and-the-ford-lightning-transformed-pickups/) , a desert-bashing[Ford F-150 Raptor R](https://www.hagerty.com/media/great-reads/jurassic-park-driving-every-raptor-to-celebrate-15-years-of-madness/) , or—gulp—something totally off the wall like the now-deceased Tesla Cybertruck, we do wild pickups better than anywhere else in the world.


Hagerty Marketplace | Eden Hitzke


Hagerty Marketplace | Eden Hitzke


But even among this crowd, the[Dodge Ram SRT-10](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/the-third-gen-dodge-viper-and-ram-srt-10-are-an-old-time-good-time/) stands out. The folks at Chrysler’s Street & Racing Technology ([SRT](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/stellantis-new-model-pipeline-srt-jeep-dodge-ram/) ) group were absolutely on a roll back in the early 2000s. Imagine being the half-ton Ram platform manager at the time; most of your product and engineering considerations probably fall toward farmers and tradesmen. Then the SRT gurus come bursting through your door one day, eyes twitching, with a proposal: “What if we took your workaday half-ton and *stuffed a Viper V-10 in it* ?”


Hagerty Marketplace | Eden Hitzke


The resulting pickup was appropriately bonkers. Aggressive street styling, a spoiler on the bed, massive brakes, lowered suspension, and a six-speed manual—the thing looked like it was doing a burnout standing still. It also went like hell. For more than two decades, the 500-hp Ram SRT-10 held the title of fastest production pickup, hitting 154.587 mph on a flying kilometer run. (Only recently did it pass that mantle on to—you guessed it—[another Ram](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ram-goes-full-send-with-rumble-bee-sport-trucks/) .)


Hagerty Marketplace | Eden Hitzke


Hagerty Marketplace | Eden Hitzke


The sheer audacity of the thing made it instantly collectible, which is why this 2004 Ram SRT-10,[currently available on Hagerty Marketplace](https://www.hagerty.com/marketplace/auction/2004-Dodge-Ram/92f9b8bd-24a9-4852-82f0-78ffa60dd82a) , caught our attention. Keen eyes may recognize this truck. It recently appeared on an episode of[Jason Cammisa’s Icons](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F4-RPcSGVFI) show, where it ripped burnouts and helped our dear host eulogize the V-10 engine.


Hagerty Marketplace | Eden Hitzke


After filming wrapped, the truck was sent to 408 Garage in San Jose, California, where the shop replaced the stock 8.3-liter V-10 with a Stage 2 Viper 8.3-liter crate engine from Prefix Corporation, a leading name in the Viper space. (Additional context on this swap can be found on the listing page.)


Hagerty Marketplace | Eden Hitzke


Factory equipment includes 22-inch forged aluminum wheels, a Dana 60 rear axle with a limited-slip differential, four-wheel disc brakes with ABS, power adjustable pedals, suede-trimmed leather bucket seats, and an Infinity audio system. In addition to the new engine, which the listing says has just 250 miles or so on it, the truck also comes with four new Michelin tires installed roughly 200 miles ago.


Hagerty Marketplace | Eden Hitzke


Hagerty Marketplace | Eden Hitzke


Hagerty Marketplace | Eden Hitzke


If you’ve ever felt like you needed a rowdy pickup in your life, this hotted-up example may be your remedy. The auction will conclude next Thursday, November 19.
